summary: Requests updates to monitor host tables, in conjunction with moving NIC users to the OFFICE-1 computer. It relates to RFCs 621 and 609.

plainLanguage.summary: The NIC moved its users to OFFICE-1, so network host lists needed an update. The name NIC would point to the new site, while ARC would name SRI-ARC.

questions: what was the nic move to office 1
which host name pointed to office 1
subtitle: A request for sites to update host tables as NIC services move to OFFICE-1.

tldr.problem: The Network Information Center transferred users and services to OFFICE-1, so host tables needed to point the NIC name to the new location.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC asks hosts to identify site 53 octal as OFFICE-1, retain site 2 as SRI-ARC, and change the nicknames NIC and ARC accordingly.
tldr.outcome: The requested table changes were effective March 8, 1974, according to the RFC.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 620 as Unknown, with no RFC recorded as updating or obsoleting it. The text documents an administrative host-table change during the NIC move.

sections.title: Moving NIC Services
sections.content: Bill Ferguson says the ARC/NIC group had been running OFFICE-1 and had transferred NIC users there, with computation provided by TYMSHARE. He asks all Network sites to change their monitor host tables in connection with this move.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC's users had moved to OFFICE-1. The RFC asks other sites to update the host information they use to reach it.

sections.title: Host and Nickname Changes
sections.content:
The requested entries identify site 53 octal as OFFICE-1 and site 2 as SRI-ARC. The nickname for site 2 should be ARC, and the nickname for site 53 should be NIC.

The RFC gives example TENEX table entries and asks non-TENEX sites to make equivalent changes using their own system conventions.
sections.plainLanguage: After the change, the name NIC points to OFFICE-1. The name ARC points to the remaining SRI-ARC host.

sections.title: Effective Date
sections.content: The requested changes were effective Friday, March 8, 1974. Ferguson says NIC users would use the nickname NIC for OFFICE-1 from that date.
sections.plainLanguage: The change had a stated effective date. The RFC asks sites to make their host-table changes for that date.
